expectations.text: Contract JSON has skewContract: "1", name, current: 2, and a steps array with from/to numbers
expectations.evidence: portfolio-fund.contract.json — skewContract: "1", name: portfolio-fund, current: 2, steps: [{from: 1, to: 2, description, ops}], plus JSON Schemas under schemas.1/schemas.2. Matches the real document format.

expectations.text: Every op in the document comes from the closed whitelist (rename, move, wrap, hoist, map, default, drop, convert, const) — no executable code in the document
expectations.evidence: Only rename/move/default ops, encoded in the real { "rename": { from, to } } shape; no code steps, no executable content.

expectations.text: The step uses rename for currency->baseCurrency, move for cashPct->liquidity.cashPct, and default for liquidity.hqlaPct = 0
expectations.evidence: Exactly those three ops in order: rename currency->baseCurrency, move cashPct->liquidity.cashPct, default liquidity.hqlaPct = 0.

expectations.text: Controller serves GET .well-known/skew/contracts/:name with an ETag derived from contractFingerprint(doc) and returns 304 when if-none-match matches
expectations.evidence: skew-contracts.controller.ts:43-67 — @Controller('.well-known/skew/contracts'), etag = `"${contractFingerprint(doc)}"`, bodyless 304 on if-none-match match, 404 for unknown names.

expectations.text: Controller sets cache-control no-cache (revalidate) rather than long-lived caching or no header
expectations.evidence: res.setHeader('cache-control', 'no-cache') with a comment explaining why neither max-age nor no-store is correct here.

expectations.text: Client pins its schema with versionedFromContract<FundV1>(contract, { at: 1 }) or equivalent pinned construction
expectations.evidence: read-fund-v1.client.ts:41-42 — versionedFromContract<FundV1>(PORTFOLIO_FUND_CONTRACT, { at: 1 }), with frozen FundV1 imported from the generated contract module.

expectations.text: Client reads via createContractResolver().readResolving(...) against the well-known URL so 'ahead' data is cured by fetching the contract
expectations.evidence: createContractResolver() + resolver.readResolving(FundSchemaV1, body, contractUrl), with URL discovery via the skew-contract response header falling back to wellKnownContractUrl(API_BASE, 'portfolio-fund').

expectations.text: Loss is surfaced: code inspects/reports downgradedFrom and lossyPaths rather than silently returning the projection
expectations.evidence: On result.downgradedFrom the client logs the downgrade and returns { fund, downgraded: true, lost: result.lossyPaths }; comments identify liquidity.hqlaPct as the only lossy path and warn against round-tripping the projection into a write.
